label: q1-mechanisms
topic: Q1 enhancer-promoter specificity: mechanisms that break the ranking
summary: Mechanisms that can change enhancer rank order are those adding a second hidden dimension beyond one enhancer strength: core-promoter motif compatibility (TATA, DPE, Inr, CpG; housekeeping versus developmental), cofactor-promoter compatibility, and TF preferences. Saturation, power-law responsiveness and promoter-independent distance or contact effects are monotone functions of one strength; a compiled core-Lean theorem (Q1.no_reversal) shows they can create ties but never reversals, although with noise they lower the raw rank correlation (simulated raw Spearman 0.76-0.83 with no true change). The literature disagrees: Martinez-Ara 2022 (mouse) finds over half of CREs promoter-selective; Bergman 2022 (human) finds multiplicative combination (R2 0.82) with subtle class effects; the Tan 2026 preprint finds similar rank order with promoter-specific power-law exponents. Our re-analysis of Martinez-Ara GEO GSE186265 gives noise-corrected between-promoter Spearman medians of 0.56, 0.83 and 0.62 for three loci (saturation alone predicts 1.0), so a rank-changing component exists there, with the caveats listed. One added experiment (2 contrasting promoters x 48-192 enhancers x 1-8 tandem copies x 3 replicates, scored by noise-corrected Spearman) separates the one-strength class (predicted about 1.0, flat in dose) from the compatibility class (predicted about 0.6-0.8, flat in dose). It does not separate motif from cofactor from TF compatibility, and does not test topology or promoter competition.
lay_summary: Think of an enhancer as a volume knob and a promoter as an amplifier. If every amplifier turns the same knob setting into more or less loudness, the loudest knob on one amplifier is also the loudest on the others, even if one amplifier clips at high volume. If different amplifiers listen for different things, the order of the knobs can truly flip. We proved on a computer that clipping alone can make two knobs tie but never swap places. In published mouse-cell data the order shifts by more than measurement noise allows, though studies disagree on how much. One extra experiment would tell the stories apart: turn each enhancer up in steps on two contrasting promoters and repeat every measurement three times.

findings.claim: In vivo, some Drosophila enhancers are specific for DPE-containing versus TATA-containing core promoters (position-matched reporter lines).
findings.evidence_quote: These studies revealed transcriptional enhancers that are specific for promoters that contain either DPE or TATA box elements.

findings.claim: Thousands of Drosophila enhancers show marked specificity for one of two core promoters (a ribosomal-protein-gene promoter versus a developmentally regulated TF promoter).
findings.evidence_quote: thousands of enhancers in Drosophila melanogaster S2 and ovarian somatic cells (OSCs) exhibit a marked specificity to one of two core promoters

findings.claim: The housekeeping/developmental enhancer split is linked to different transcription factors: Dref activates housekeeping, Trl developmental enhancers.
findings.evidence_quote: we identify two transcription factors--Dref and Trl--that bind and activate housekeeping versus developmental enhancers, respectively.

findings.claim: Core-promoter responsiveness to one strong enhancer spans several orders of magnitude across Drosophila sequences (a promoter-side axis).
findings.evidence_quote: In the presence of a single strong enhancer, the enhancer responsiveness of different sequences differs by several orders of magnitude

findings.claim: Transcriptional cofactors differ in which core-promoter types they activate (cofactor-promoter compatibility).
findings.evidence_quote: We observe differential activation of CPs, indicating distinct regulatory preferences or 'compatibilities' between COFs and specific types of CPs.

findings.claim: In human K562 ExP STARR-seq (1,000 enhancers x 1,000 promoters), enhancer and promoter activities combine multiplicatively; most enhancers activate all promoters by similar amounts.
findings.evidence_quote: most enhancers activate all promoters by similar amounts, and intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities multiplicatively combine to determine RNA output (R2 = 0.82).

findings.claim: Bergman et al.: housekeeping promoters carry built-in activating motifs (GABPA, YY1) that lower responsiveness to distal enhancers (a ceiling-like promoter-side effect).
findings.evidence_quote: Promoters of housekeeping genes contain built-in activating motifs for factors such as GABPA and YY1, which decrease the responsiveness of promoters to distal enhancers.

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara et al. (mouse cells, thousands of CRE-promoter pairs) emphasise the opposite: most CREs are promoter-selective.
findings.evidence_quote: More than half of the tested CREs exhibit significant promoter selectivity.

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara et al.: selectivity does not track native looping, so compatibility and folding are separate axes.
findings.evidence_quote: CRE-promoter selectivity does not correlate with looping interactions in the native genomic context

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara et al. note a saturation-like pattern and say it cannot be told apart from lower enhancer dependence of high-basal promoters.
findings.evidence_quote: This suggests a saturation effect, or it could indicate that promoters with high basal activity are less dependent on distal enhancers.

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara et al.: strong boosting occurs mostly at low-basal promoters.
findings.evidence_quote: Strong boosting occurred primarily at promoters with low basal activities, while highly active promoters were more difficult to boost

findings.claim: Tan et al. 2026 preprint says earlier reporter assays disagree because of assay confounders and finds a similar enhancer rank order across promoters (abstract only; full text blocked by HTTP 429).
findings.evidence_quote: Promoters differ in their responsiveness to enhancers (>100-fold versus 1.1-fold activation) while enhancers activate all promoters in a similar rank order.

findings.claim: Tan et al.: promoter output follows a power law in enhancer activity with a promoter-specific exponent (a promoter-specific monotone response, rank-preserving by construction).
findings.evidence_quote: Promoter output scales with enhancer activity following a power law, with the exponent varying across promoters.

findings.claim: Tan et al.: responsiveness is modulated by core-promoter TF motifs.
findings.evidence_quote: Responsiveness is modulated by transcription factor motifs in the core promoter.

findings.claim: Enhancer effect depends nonlinearly on enhancer-promoter contact probability.
findings.evidence_quote: the transcriptional effect of an enhancer depends on its contact probabilities with the promoter through a nonlinear relationship.

findings.claim: Zuin et al. best-fit Hill coefficient for burst frequency versus contact probability is 2.8.
findings.evidence_quote: Hill coefficient ( h ) of 2.8 (95% confidence interval = 2.4-3.2

findings.claim: Enhancer needs cohesin only for activating distant genes (distance/topology axis).
findings.evidence_quote: It requires cohesin exclusively for the activation of distant genes, not of proximal genes

findings.claim: SPIE-seq (preprint): enhancer influence decays with distance with similar average scaling for all enhancers.
findings.evidence_quote: enhancer influence declines with genomic distance, following similar average distance-decay scaling across all tested enhancers

findings.claim: SPIE-seq: promoter skipping grows as competitors accumulate, so promoters do not respond independently (invisible in single-promoter reporters).
findings.evidence_quote: Promoter skipping is common and increases as competitors accumulate

findings.claim: Strong enhancers behave sub-additively because of competition with the target promoter; weak ones additively (Drosophila embryo).
findings.evidence_quote: weakly active enhancers function additively while strong enhancers behave sub-additively due to competition with the target promoter.

findings.claim: A product of activity and contact (ABC) predicts CRISPRi enhancer-gene links better than earlier methods (a one-strength-times-contact model).
findings.evidence_quote: a simple activity-by-contact model substantially outperformed previous methods at predicting the complex connections in our CRISPR dataset.

findings.claim: In mouse ESC loci, developmental genes insulate regulatory domains partly by promoter competition rather than enhancer blocking.
findings.evidence_quote: developmental genes preferentially contribute to regulatory insulation through non-structural mechanisms involving promoter competition rather than enhancer blocking.

findings.claim: Theory: burst frequency and burst size rise with E-P communication strength as power laws.
findings.evidence_quote: burst frequency and burst size are up-regulated by E-P communication strength, following power laws with positive exponents.

findings.claim: A native-locus enhancer (eNMU) shows a hierarchy: autonomous enhancer e1 dominates facilitators and the promoter.
findings.evidence_quote: The autonomous enhancer e1 is functionally hierarchical to e2, additional facilitators, and the NMU promoter

findings.claim: Lean 4 (core only, no Mathlib, v4.35.0), compiled with exit 0: if every promoter responds to one enhancer strength through a non-decreasing function (any saturation, Hill, power law), a strict order on one promoter can never become the opposite strict order on another (Q1.no_reversal); with strictly increasing responses strict order is kept (Q1.strict_preserved); a two-latent model reverses order (Q1.two_latent_reverses). So saturation alone creates ties, never reversals.

findings.claim: Re-analysis of Martinez-Ara GSE186265 upstream EP matrix, locus Klf2 (69 cCREs x 22 promoters, 1344 observed cells): replicate-disattenuated Spearman between promoter pairs has median 0.56 (10-90% 0.37-0.83; raw median 0.36; 231 promoter pairs). Pure saturation predicts 1.0. 5-fold CV R2 on log10 activity: additive 0.938; one-latent+per-promoter-monotone 0.923; additive+rank1 interaction 0.943; rank2 0.942; replicate-noise ceiling 0.968; gap additive-to-ceiling 0.030.

Re-analysis of Martinez-Ara GSE186265 upstream EP matrix, locus Nanog (29 cCREs x 11 promoters, 294 observed cells): replicate-disattenuated Spearman between promoter pairs has median 0.83 (10-90% 0.51-1.00; raw median 0.60; 29 promoter pairs). Pure saturation predicts 1.0. 5-fold CV R2 on log10 activity: additive 0.859; one-latent+per-promoter-monotone 0.845; additive+rank1 interaction 0.862; rank2 0.869; replicate-noise ceiling 0.930; gap additive-to-ceiling 0.071.

Re-analysis of Martinez-Ara GSE186265 upstream EP matrix, locus Tfcp2l1 (145 cCREs x 21 promoters, 2304 observed cells): replicate-disattenuated Spearman between promoter pairs has median 0.62 (10-90% 0.42-0.74; raw median 0.49; 190 promoter pairs). Pure saturation predicts 1.0. 5-fold CV R2 on log10 activity: additive 0.842; one-latent+per-promoter-monotone 0.855; additive+rank1 interaction 0.860; rank2 0.856; replicate-noise ceiling 0.985; gap additive-to-ceiling 0.144.

Simulation (assumed: SD of log10 enhancer strength 0.5; noise 0.10 log10 on a 3-replicate mean; promoter A Hill K=10^1.5, basal 1, headroom 100x; promoter B basal 30, headroom 10x, K=1; 48 enhancers; 1,2,4,8 copies): saturation-only gives RAW Spearman between promoters 0.76 [0.60,0.87] / 0.82 [0.71,0.90] / 0.82 [0.71,0.90] / 0.77 [0.62,0.88] at 1/2/4/8 copies (mean [95% interval]) although no order changes, but replicate-disattenuated Spearman 1.00 [0.85,1.16] / 0.99 [0.87,1.10] / 0.99 [0.87,1.10] / 0.98 [0.82,1.15]. Two-latent models at 2 copies give disattenuated 0.82 [0.60,0.98] (latent r=cos34deg=0.83) and 0.58 [0.30,0.83] (r=cos53deg=0.60). So saturation can mimic a low raw rank correlation; it cannot mimic a low disattenuated one.

findings.claim: Same simulation with 192 enhancers at 2 copies (300 repeats): disattenuated Spearman saturation-only 0.99 [0.93,1.04]; latent r=0.83 0.80 [0.72,0.88]; latent r=0.60 0.58 [0.46,0.69]. Intervals separate even for the mild case; with 48 enhancers the r=0.83 case (0.82 [0.60,0.98]) overlaps saturation-only (0.99 [0.87,1.10]).

key_claims.claim: Reporter-assay studies disagree. Martinez-Ara (mouse) finds most CREs promoter-selective.
key_claims.evidence_quote: More than half of the tested CREs exhibit significant promoter selectivity.

key_claims.claim: Bergman (human) finds most enhancers activate all promoters similarly and activities combine multiplicatively (R2 0.82). Tan 2026 preprint reports a similar rank order with promoter-specific power-law exponents.
key_claims.evidence_quote: most enhancers activate all promoters by similar amounts, and intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities multiplicatively combine to determine RNA output (R2 = 0.82).

key_claims.claim: Martinez-Ara themselves say their basal-activity trend cannot separate saturation from lower enhancer dependence, so published data leave saturation versus compatibility open.
key_claims.evidence_quote: This suggests a saturation effect, or it could indicate that promoters with high basal activity are less dependent on distal enhancers.

key_claims.claim: Saturation (any monotone promoter response to one enhancer strength) can tie enhancer order but not reverse it, so a reversal needs a second latent (compatibility). Proved in compiled core Lean; in the Martinez-Ara data replicate-disattenuated Spearman is 0.56 (Klf2), 0.83 (Nanog), 0.62 (Tfcp2l1) instead of 1.

could_not_find: Full texts of Bergman 2022, Haberle 2019 and Zabidi 2015 (not open access via Europe PMC, HTTP 500): only abstracts were read; the ExP STARR-seq matrix was not re-analysed.

Full texts of the Tan et al. 2026 and SPIE-seq 2026 bioRxiv preprints: bioRxiv returned HTTP 429 (Cloudflare 1015). Only abstracts were read, so the power-law exponents and rank-correlation values are unknown to us. Both are unreviewed preprints.

Any direct measurement of enhancer-order change under copy-number titration: none found. The predicted numbers are simulations under stated assumptions (SD 0.5 log10, noise 0.10 log10, Hill n=1, dose acting as multiplicative strength), not measurements.

In the Martinez-Ara re-analysis the disattenuated Spearman includes inactive cCREs near the floor and averages over fragment orientation (floor 0.02); CV R2 differences between models are 2 percentage points or less with only 294-2304 observed cells, so the low-rank model comparison is weak and only the sub-1 disattenuated Spearman is claimed.
Dedicated papers on human Inr/DPE-specific enhancer effects and a mammalian cofactor-degron rank-change experiment were not located. OpenAlex was not used, per rules.
The delphisci lean registry was only listed (read-only), not built; no Mathlib build was run. A core-only Lean file in the scripts folder was compiled instead.

recommendations: Run the proposed experiment: 2 contrasting promoters x at least 48 enhancers (192 to resolve a mild rank change) x 1,2,4,8 tandem copies x 3 independent replicates, same backbone, position and cell type; score with replicate-disattenuated Spearman, not raw Spearman (saturation alone gives raw 0.76-0.83 in simulation).

Decision rule: a disattenuated Spearman whose 95% interval includes 1.0 and is flat in copy number supports one strength plus a monotone promoter response (saturation, responsiveness, power law, promoter-independent distance or contact). A value clearly below 1 (0.6-0.8 in the Martinez-Ara re-analysis) that is flat in dose supports compatibility (motif, cofactor, TF).

To split compatibility sub-mechanisms (outside the one experiment): an arm that swaps or mutates TATA, DPE, Inr or CpG content in the same promoters, and a cofactor-degron arm (Mediator, BRD4 or p300 depletion). Predictions for these are qualitative only here.

To test topology and competition (also outside the one experiment): vary spacing for the same enhancers on one promoter, and add a second promoter in cis. SPIE-seq predicts similar average decay for all enhancers (no reorder) and context-dependent competition.

Reconcile the literature before relying on one study: Martinez-Ara (mouse, over half of CREs selective), Bergman (human, mostly multiplicative), Tan 2026 (similar rank order, promoter-specific exponent). Our re-analysis finds a rank-changing component in the mouse data but cannot exclude the assay confounders Tan et al. describe.
